einzeiler: The 1933 kidnapping of ten-year-old Peggy McMath by local resident Kenneth Buck.
kurzfassung: In May 1933, ten-year-old Peggy McMath was abducted from her school in Harwich, Massachusetts, by an unemployed local named Kenneth Buck. Buck orchestrated the kidnapping to demand a ransom, utilizing a poorly executed disguise and involving his brother to deliver the demands. Following her safe return after a 60-hour ordeal, Buck was apprehended, convicted, and sentenced to 25 years in prison.
stichpunkte: Kidnapping became a prominent and alarming trend in the United States during the Great Depression due to financially motivated ransoms.
Kenneth Buck, an unemployed former chauffeur from Harwich, Massachusetts, decided to kidnap ten-year-old Peggy McMath after failing to secure a job at her family's estate.
On May 2, 1933, Buck used a crude soot disguise to deceive a school official and abducted Peggy outside Harwich Center School.
Buck held the young girl captive in an isolated shack while maintaining a remarkably casual routine, including playing a round of golf with a friend.
To handle the ransom negotiations without exposing himself, Buck enlisted his brother Cyril to act as a go-between with the McMath family.
Following a high-stakes exchange on a boat, Peggy was safely returned to her father, and authorities swiftly arrested Cyril and Kenneth Buck.
During the June 1933 trial, despite an unexpectedly lighthearted courtroom atmosphere, Kenneth Buck was found guilty and sentenced to 25 years in a work camp.
Peggy McMath grew up, served in the Navy near the end of World War II, and lived a private life until her death in 2014 at the age of 91.

clips.hook: Kidnappings reported alongside births and deaths
clips.text: Major print publications regularly featured updates on abductions right alongside standard family announcements.

clips.hook: Using burnt cork as a bizarre disguise
clips.text: The perpetrator attempted to alter his appearance by rubbing soot from burned cork onto his face.

clips.hook: Playing golf immediately after abducting a child
clips.text: Shortly after locking a young girl in a remote shack, the abductor casually met up with an acquaintance to play a round of golf.

clips.hook: Demanding millions during the Great Depression
clips.text: The initial ransom demand amounted to a massive sum that would translate to millions of dollars today.

clips.hook: Believing he was a criminal mastermind
clips.text: The kidnapper wore an elaborate and ridiculous combination of items while believing his identity was completely secure.

beschreibung:
On May 2, 1933, the Harwich Center School received a telephone call from the father of ten-year-old Peggy McMath, a student at the school. Mr. McMath informed them that he was sending a driver to pick up his daughter and he expected her to be ready. However, when the driver showed up, Peggy didn’t recognize the man and was hesitant to get into the car. In response, the driver of the car, Kenneth Buck, grabbed the girl, threw her in the car, and drove off before anyone could stop him.
